part.backRankMate.title: Back-rank mate
part.backRankMate.summary: A king trapped behind its own pawns gets mated on the back rank; before the check, count who defends the rank.
ex.br.tTluB: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.br.tTluB.hint: The black king on h8 is trapped by its pawns. See whether Black's back rank has a defender.
ex.br.tTluB.solution: 37.Qxe8#! The queen captures the rook on e8 with check. The pawns on g7 and h7 trap the king, and no black piece can recapture.
ex.br.BaN01: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.br.BaN01.hint: The white king on g1 is behind the pawns on f2, g2 and h2. Look for the rook check on the first rank.
ex.br.BaN01.solution: 22...Re1#! The rook checks down the e-file. The king has no square: f1 is watched by the rook and by the knight on d2, and no white piece can block.
ex.br.x4aZI: Play as White and find the best move. Black threatens your king, but it is your move.
ex.br.x4aZI.hint: Before defending, see whether the black king has an escape square.
ex.br.x4aZI.solution: 31.Qd8#! The queen reaches the eighth rank along the diagonal and gives check. The pawns on f7, g7 and h7 trap the king, and no black piece can block.
ex.br.sbhpt: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.br.sbhpt.hint: White's first rank has no defender. Look for the queen's way there.
ex.br.sbhpt.solution: 24...Qd1#! The queen reaches the first rank along the diagonal and gives check. The white king is trapped by its pawns, and the bishop on b3 cannot capture the queen, because the pawn on c2 is in the way.
ex.br.ZBohs: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.br.ZBohs.hint: Count who attacks and who defends e1: the queen and the rook are on the same file.
ex.br.ZBohs.solution: 19...Qxe1+! The queen captures the rook on e1 with check. The knight on d3 is the only defender and recaptures with 20.Nxe1, and then 20...Rxe1# is mate.
ex.br.GGN2D: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.br.GGN2D.hint: The rook on e8 has only one defender. How many of your pieces attack that square?
ex.br.GGN2D.solution: 20.Qxe8+! The queen captures the rook on e8 with check. The black queen recaptures with 20...Qxe8, and 21.Rxe8# is mate: the rank is left without a defender.
ex.br.pw0ey: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.br.pw0ey.hint: Give check on the first rank. If a piece blocks, see whether anything defends it.
ex.br.pw0ey.solution: 30...Qa1+! The queen checks on the first rank, and the white king has no square. The white queen blocks with 31.Qb1, with no defender, and 31...Qxb1# is mate.
ex.br.XY3hX: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.br.XY3hX.hint: Before using the back rank, see which white piece defends f1.
ex.br.XY3hX.solution: 36...Ne2+! The knight checks and attacks the rook on g3. The king, which defended f1, only has h1. After 37.Kh1, 37...Rf1# is a back-rank mate: the rook watches g1, and the pawns on g2 and h2 trap the king.
part.queenRookMates.title: Queen and rook mates
part.queenRookMates.summary: Two heavy pieces on neighbouring ranks, or the supported queen next to the king, mate a king on the edge; before the check, look at the support.
ex.qr.THeY6: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.qr.THeY6.hint: Your rook on e7 already closes the seventh rank. Look for the check on the eighth.
ex.qr.THeY6.solution: 37.Rf8#! The rook on f1 checks along the eighth rank, and the one on e7 closes the seventh: it is the ladder. The bishop on h7 covers g8, and no black piece can capture the rook.
ex.qr.MS4Re: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.qr.MS4Re.hint: The white king is on the h-file, and your rook on g6 closes the g-file.
ex.qr.MS4Re.solution: 22...Rh5#! The rook on d5 checks along the h-file, and the one on g6 closes the g-file: it is the ladder, on neighbouring files. The pawn on h2 blocks the king's last square.
ex.qr.eTWci: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.qr.eTWci.hint: Look for the square next to the white king that your knight supports.
ex.qr.eTWci.solution: 26...Qh2#! The queen checks on h2, next to the king, and the knight on g4 supports it. The queen covers h1, the knight covers f2, and the white pieces on f1 and g2 block the rest.
ex.qr.llCQP: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.qr.llCQP.hint: The pawn on h6 is defended only by the king. How many of your pieces attack that square?
ex.qr.llCQP.solution: 39.Qxh6#! The queen captures the pawn on h6 with check, next to the king, and the rook on g6 supports it. The king has no square: the rook covers g7 and g8, and the queen covers h8.
ex.qr.nx5Gi: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.qr.nx5Gi.hint: Your pawns on h5 and h6 are close to the black king. Which squares do they support?
ex.qr.nx5Gi.solution: 24.Qg6+! The queen checks on g6, supported by the pawn on h5, and the king only has h8. After 24...Kh8, 25.Qg7# is mate: the queen stands next to the king, supported by the pawn on h6.
ex.qr.fd4Y9: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.qr.fd4Y9.hint: The white king is on the first rank. See which rank your rook on b2 can close.
ex.qr.fd4Y9.solution: 44...Rxg2+! The rook captures the knight on g2 with check, and the white king only has f1. After 45.Kf1, 45...Rh1# is mate: the rook on g2 closes the second rank, and the one on h8 checks on the first. It is the ladder.
ex.qr.r6AsE: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.qr.r6AsE.hint: Your rook on e7 supports the squares of the seventh rank, close to the black king.
ex.qr.r6AsE.solution: 36.Qf7+! The queen checks on f7, supported by the rook on e7, and the king only has h8. After 36...Kh8, 37.Qh7# is mate: the queen stands next to the king, supported by the rook again.
ex.qr.mMJXe: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.qr.mMJXe.hint: Your knight on d2 watches f1 and f3. Look for the check that brings the white king close to it.
ex.qr.mMJXe.solution: 32...Qb1+! The queen checks along the first rank, and the king only has g2. After 33.Kg2, 33...Qf1# is mate: the queen stands next to the king, supported by the knight on d2, which also covers f3. The pawn on f2 blocks the white queen.
ex.qr.6MGGU: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.qr.6MGGU.hint: Your bishop on g7 watches the diagonal up to b2. Look for the check that brings the white king close to it.
ex.qr.6MGGU.solution: 14...Qa3+! The queen checks along the diagonal, and the king only has b1. After 15.Kb1, 15...Qb2# is mate: the queen goes to b2, next to the king, supported by the bishop on g7, and covers a1 and c1. The pawn on c2 blocks the white queen.
part.rookBishopMates.title: Rook and bishop mates
part.rookBishopMates.summary: The rook checks and the bishop helps: it either supports the rook next to the king (Opera mate) or takes the escape square from the king (Pillsbury's mate).
ex.rb.FzQZy: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.rb.FzQZy.hint: Your bishop on g7 watches the long diagonal up to a1.
ex.rb.FzQZy.solution: 29...Ra1#! The rook checks on a1, next to the king, and the bishop on g7 supports it and covers b2. The rook on c8 takes c2 from the king: it is the Opera mate.
ex.rb.4vLTZ: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.rb.4vLTZ.hint: The square h2, next to the white king, is free. Who watches it?
ex.rb.4vLTZ.solution: 39...Re1#! The rook checks from afar, along the first rank, and the bishop on d6 covers h2, the escape square: it is Pillsbury's mate. No white piece reaches f1 or e1.
ex.rb.CvBwJ: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.rb.CvBwJ.hint: Look at the squares your bishop on h6 watches.
ex.rb.CvBwJ.solution: 34.Rxf8#! The rook captures the bishop on f8 with check, next to the king, and the bishop on h6 supports it and covers g7: it is the Opera mate.
ex.rb.nlMjk: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.rb.nlMjk.hint: The white king has few squares. Which check takes almost all of them away?
ex.rb.nlMjk.solution: 29...Bh3+! The bishop checks and covers f1 and g2, and the king only has g1. After 30.Kg1, 30...Re1# is mate: the rook checks from afar, along the first rank, and the bishop on h3 covers f1 and g2. The pawns on f2 and h2 hem the king in: it is Pillsbury's mate.
ex.rb.AROjF: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.rb.AROjF.hint: Look for a bishop check that leaves the white king a single square.
ex.rb.AROjF.solution: 35...Bd6+! The bishop checks and covers e5, and the king only has g5. After 36.Kg5, 36...Rg8# is mate: the rook checks from afar, the bishop covers f4, the rook on h3 closes the h-file, and the king on f7 covers f6 and g6.
ex.rb.XD8qk: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.rb.XD8qk.hint: The rook on e8 is the only black piece defending the eighth rank.
ex.rb.XD8qk.solution: 24.Qxe8+! The queen captures the rook with check, and the bishop on d7 captures it. After 24...Bxe8, 25.Rxe8# is mate: the rook checks from afar, and the bishop on d3 covers h7, the escape square. It is Pillsbury's mate.
ex.rb.5iU9s: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.rb.5iU9s.hint: The rook on g8 defends f8, the square your bishop on d6 watches.
ex.rb.5iU9s.solution: 30.Qxg8+! The queen captures the rook on g8 with check, and the king has to capture it. After 30...Kxg8, 31.Rf8# is mate: the rook stands next to the king, supported by the bishop on d6. The rook on g8 defended f8, and the queen removed it: it is the Opera mate.
ex.rb.aih2N: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.rb.aih2N.hint: The white rook on f1 defends e1, the square your bishop on d2 watches.
ex.rb.aih2N.solution: 29...Qxf1+! The queen captures the rook on f1 with check, and the king has to capture it. After 30.Kxf1, 30...Re1# is mate: the rook stands next to the king, supported by the bishop on d2, and the pawns on f2 and g2 hem the king in. The rook on f1 defended e1, and the queen removed it.
